questions.q: Report: 'Where did you go?' she asked me.
questions.a: 'She asked me where I had gone.' wh-word kept, 'did' deleted, order restored, went→had gone. A wrong answer 'where did I go' inside the frame reveals the student quotes the question verbatim — the core failure this node exists to fix.

questions.q: Report: 'Do you like tea?' he asked.
questions.a: 'He asked (me) if/whether I liked tea.' yes/no needs if/whether, do-support removed, like→liked. A wrong answer 'he asked did I like tea' shows the student has no de-interrogation step — the question grammar survives intact into reporting.

questions.q: Which is correct: 'She asked me that where was I going' or 'She asked me where I was going'?
questions.a: The second — 'that' cannot join a wh-question, and 'where was I' keeps question order. A wrong answer choosing the first reveals the student thinks 'that' is the universal reported-speech glue, regardless of sentence type.

What is Reported questions lose their question grammar? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Reported questions lose their question grammar: no question mark, no do/does/did, and statement word order returns. 'Where do you live?' → 'He asked where I lived.' Yes/no questions take 'if/whether'; wh-questions keep the wh-word as connector.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Reported questions lose their question grammar?
questions.a: Students keep question order inside reported frames ('He asked where did I live'), keep the question mark, or use 'if' for wh-questions ('asked if where I lived').

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student reports wh-questions and yes/no questions with correct connector choice, restored statement order, and removed do-support, and can spot the residual question mark error.
